selection: step-out from bonsai1/L34/N1406+ (10x queue, model pilot: sonnet)

neighbours.label: the 'inv-' piece of invite words (Inv|ites, un|inv|ited, _inv|ites): fires on the split piece before '-ited/-ites'
fire: Download our free printable Birthday Invitations for your next party.
Several uninvited guests wandered into the wedding reception.
Only Invited speakers may present at the closing session.
Spread the news with our elegant Wedding Invites online.
Nobody likes feeling uninvited at the office holiday gathering.
Reply to the Invitation card by the end of the month.
quiet: Download our free printable Birthday Cards for your next party.
Several unexpected guests wandered into the wedding reception.
Only keynote speakers may present at the closing session.
Spread the news with our elegant Wedding Menus online.
Nobody likes feeling ignored at the office holiday gathering.

notes: Model pilot (sonnet arm; the same pole is tested independently by the other arm, pairing disclosed): this pole feeds the held pole bonsai1/L34/N1406+ (zeroing this neuron removes 0.65 of the anchor's peak), from a batched edge measurement with 8 same-layer placebos. Label and all 16 sentences written by the Sonnet 5.5 labeller from a packet (card + all-pole band samples + the edge hint) and one probe round of 8 sentences (none reused). An Opus gate checked rule-level items only and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Probes: only the explicit ' Inv' piece scored well (0.74); prediction-style contexts ('was pointedly not', 'cordially') were 0.06-0.26, so I label the piece, not the prediction. Fire items therefore contain the invite word; near misses swap it for a plain noun.
